module.title: Materials, Textures & Possessions: Whose is this?
module.group: A2.2 - Social Dynamics, Work & Everyday Life
module.objective: Describe physical objects, materials, textures, and clarify ownership using possessive pronouns and 'whose'.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Materials, Textures and Possessions
subModules.grammarFocus: be made of, whose, possessive pronouns, belong to
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Materials and textures such as leather, cotton, plastic, metal, wood, wool, glass, silk

content.summary: Welcome to our reading mission about everyday objects, materials, and possessions. In this module, you will read short texts about items found at school, find out what different things are made of, and learn how to talk about who owns them using clear grammar patterns.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Describing object materials with made of, asking and answering questions about ownership with whose, possessive pronouns, and belong to.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Common materials such as wood, metal, cotton, leather, wool, glass, silk, and words related to textures and belongings.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts for specific material names and skimming paragraphs to identify object owners.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 texts about everyday objects and materials.
Locate specific details such as material types and owner names in reading passages.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with whose, possessive pronouns, and made of.

contextWarmup.prompt: Look at your jacket or shirt right now. What is it usually made of?
options: It is made of soft cotton or wool.
It is made of solid glass and metal.
It is made of heavy oak wood.
contextWarmup.explanation: Clothing items are normally made of fabrics like cotton or wool, not glass, metal, or wood.

rules: Rule 1: Use be plus made of followed by the material name to describe what an object consists of, such as The table is made of wood.
Rule 2: Use Whose followed by a noun and be to ask about ownership, for example, Whose jacket is this?
Rule 3: Use possessive pronouns like mine, yours, his, hers, ours, and theirs to answer ownership questions without repeating the noun.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use from instead of of when describing materials, or mix up possessive adjectives with possessive pronouns.
commonTrap.wrong: This bag is made from leather and it is my.
commonTrap.correct: This bag is made of leather and it is mine.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Material Descriptions
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practice affirmative, negative, and question forms:

items.exampleSentence: My jacket is made of leather.
This T-shirt is made of cotton.
The bottle is made of plastic.
The gate is made of metal.
The chair is made of wood.
Her sweater is made of wool.
The vase is made of glass.
That scarf is made of silk.
The fabric has a soft texture.

paragraphs: At Green Valley School, the lost and found box is always full of interesting items at the end of the week. Students leave their jackets, water bottles, and notebooks in the classrooms, and the teachers collect them. On Friday afternoon, Mr. Davis opens the box on his desk so students can find their missing belongings.

Sarah walks to the front of the classroom and looks inside the box. She picks up a soft red scarf. She asks, Whose scarf is this? Liam smiles and answers, It is mine. My grandmother made it of pure wool for my birthday. Next, Sarah holds up a small blue bottle. And whose bottle is this? she asks. That plastic bottle belongs to me, says Chloe, raising her hand quickly.

Finally, Mr. Davis pulls out a heavy wooden box with a smooth texture. He asks the class whose box it is. No one says anything at first. Then Alex remembers and shouts, Oh, that belongs to the art club! It is made of old oak wood. Everyone laughs and collects their items before the weekend starts.

content.summary: Practical guide on writing clear sentences about object materials, textures, and ownership using correct grammar and punctuation.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Describing Object Materials

blueprintItems.formula: Subject + be + mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize the first letter of sentences and proper names.
mechanicsRules.badExample: whose glass window is broken in london?
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Whose glass window is broken in London?
mechanicsRules.why: Sentences always start with a capital letter, and London is a city name.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use apostrophes correctly for singular possession with names.
mechanicsRules.why: Add an apostrophe and s to a person's name to show ownership.

mechanicsRules.rule: Match demonstrative pronouns with singular and plural nouns.
mechanicsRules.why: Keys is plural, so you must use are these instead of is this.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Materials, Textures and Possessions

content.summary: This speaking lab focuses on talking about everyday objects, describing material types such as leather, cotton, and plastic, and discussing who items belong to using clear sentence structures.
content.audioGuidance: Listen closely to how material names are pronounced. Place primary stress on the first syllable for words like leather, cotton, and plastic, and keep your voice clear when asking whose items are on the table.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear short and long vowels in material nouns
pillars.explanation: Pronounce short vowels in wood and wool clearly without adding extra sounds.

pillars.name: Material Stress
pillars.explanation: Emphasize the first syllable in two-syllable material words like leather, cotton, and metal.

pillars.name: Possession Intonation
pillars.target: Rising and falling tones in questions and answers
pillars.explanation: Use rising intonation when asking whose object something is, and falling intonation when stating ownership.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that both material nouns place the primary stress on the first syllable.
Keep the first syllable strong and clear when naming soft fabric types.
Both nouns maintain firm initial syllable stress.
Stress remains firmly on the first syllable for surface feel descriptors.

sections.title: Speaking Practicum and AI Voice Evaluation

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about a favorite item you own and what material it is made of.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about an object you use every day, what material it is made of, and why you like it.
storyPoints: What the object is and what material it is made of
How often you use it during the week
Why this possession is special to you
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My favorite backpack is made of strong cotton and I use it every day.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈfeɪvərɪt ˈbækpæk ɪz meɪd ɒv strɒŋ ˈkɒtən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Speak fluently in full sentences using the Present Simple tense and material vocabulary.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Describe your bedroom, mentioning at least two materials of the furniture or objects inside.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about the furniture in your room and what materials they are made of.
storyPoints: Describe your desk and what wood or metal it uses
Mention another item like a glass window or wool rug
Explain how your room feels with these textures
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My study desk is made of wood and my floor rug is made of soft wool.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈstʌdi desk ɪz meɪd ɒv wʊd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use natural pacing and clear pronunciation when naming household items and materials.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your classmate asking about a jacket left on the desk.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your classmate asks: Whose blue cotton jacket is this on the chair? Respond and explain.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are in the classroom after lunch. A classmate holds up a jacket and asks who it belongs to.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: That blue cotton jacket belongs to me. Thank you for finding it.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðæt bluː ˈkɒtən ˈdʒækɪt bɪˈlɒŋz tuː miː/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Answer politely and state ownership clearly using 'belongs to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Ask a shop assistant about the material of a handbag.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ask the shop assistant if the brown handbag is made of real leather.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are shopping in a clothing store and want to check a product texture.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Excuse me, is this brown handbag made of real leather?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪkˈskjuːs miː, ɪz ðɪs braʊn ˈhændbæɡ meɪd ɒv riːəl ˈleðə/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use polite opening phrases and correct material vocabulary.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Reply to a friend who asks about the texture of a new sofa.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your friend asks: How does the fabric of this new sofa feel? Describe it.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are visiting a furniture store with your friend.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It has a very soft texture because it is covered in wool.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt hæz ə ˈvəri sɒft ˈtekstʃə bɪˈkɒz ɪt ɪz ˈkʌvəd ɪn wʊl/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describe the tactile feeling using descriptive adjectives and material nouns.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Explain to a relative whose metal keys you found on the table.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your uncle asks: Whose keys are these? Tell him they are yours.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at a family dinner and notice car keys on the dining table.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Those metal keys belong to me. I left them there by mistake.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Confirm ownership clearly with a polite explanation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the target sentence focusing on accurate vocabulary pronunciation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: The window is made of glass and the table is made of wood.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The window is made of glass and the table is made of wood.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈwɪndəʊ ɪz meɪd ɒv ɡlɑːs ænd ðə ˈteɪbəl ɪz meɪd ɒv wʊd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Ensure the material nouns glass and wood are pronounced clearly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice the correct grammatical structure for possession.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: This red silk scarf belongs to my mother.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: This red silk scarf belongs to my mother.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðɪs red sɪlk skɑːf bɪˈlɒŋz tuː maɪ ˈmʌðə/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Pay attention to the third-person singular verb form 'belongs'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice correct word stress on multi-syllable material and texture words.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: Leather and plastic items have a smooth texture.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Leather and plastic items have a smooth texture.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Keep primary stress on the first syllable of leather, plastic, and texture.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice rising intonation for questions and falling intonation for statements.

practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Whose metal bottle is this? It is mine.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Use rising intonation on 'whose' and falling intonation on the final statement.
